First determine the distances between consecutive points on the line.

Let  

\[
AB=a,\; BC=b,\; CD=c,\; DE=d,\; EF=e .
\]

The given data give

\[
\begin{aligned}
a+b &= 26 \quad &(AC)\\
b+c &= 22 \quad &(BD)\\
c+d &= 31 \quad &(CE)\\
d+e &= 33 \quad &(DF)\\
a+b+c+d+e &= 73 \quad &(AF)
\end{aligned}
\]

Solve the system:

\[
\begin{aligned}
b &= 26-a,\\
c &= 22-b = a-4,\\
d &= 31-c = 35-a,\\
e &= 33-d = a-2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Substituting into the last equation:

\[
a+(26-a)+(a-4)+(35-a)+(a-2)=73\;\Longrightarrow\; a=18.
\]

Thus  

\[
AB=18,\; BC=8,\; CD=14,\; DE=17,\; EF=16.
\]

Place the points on the \(x\)-axis with \(A\) at the origin:

\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=(0,0),\\
B&=(18,0),\\
C&=(26,0),\\
D&=(40,0),\\
E&=(57,0),\\
F&=(73,0).
\end{aligned}
\]

---

### Position of \(G\)

Let \(G=(x,y)\).  
Given \(CG=40\) and \(DG=30\):

\[
\begin{cases}
(x-26)^2+y^2=40^2=1600,\\
(x-40)^2+y^2=30^2=900.
\end{cases}
\]

Subtracting the equations:

\[
(x-26)^2-(x-40)^2=700
\;\Longrightarrow\; 28x-924=700
\;\Longrightarrow\; x=58.
\]

Then

\[
y^2=1600-(58-26)^2=1600-32^2=576
\;\Longrightarrow\; y=\pm24.
\]

Take \(G=(58,24)\) (the sign does not affect the area).

---

### Area of \(\triangle BGE\)

Vertices: \(B(18,0),\; G(58,24),\; E(57,0)\).

Using the shoelace formula:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area}&=\frac12\Bigl|
18(24-0)+58(0-0)+57(0-24)\Bigr|\\
&=\frac12|432-1368|\\
&=\frac12(936)=468.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus the area of \(\triangle BGE\) is  

\[
\boxed{468}.
\]
